page.title: Instance
page.purpose: Show one instance in full: where it came from, what state it is in, what it has cost, when it drains, and whether it became a trusted node.

priorities.statement: What this instance is and what it has cost so far.
When it drains, and how to extend that deliberately.
Whether enrollment succeeded, is queued, or failed.
priorities.notes: An un-enrolled instance is a normal degraded state, not an error.

priorities.statement: How to destroy it, with enough friction that it is never accidental.

states.description: Running instance with cost accruing and lifetime counting down.
Instance is running but enrollment is queued, so it is not yet a usable node.
A lifecycle transition is in flight, such as creating or draining.
Destroyed, showing the settled figure rather than a live one.
The instance could not be fetched.
The caller may view the fleet but not act on this instance.
The instance id resolves to nothing this scenario owns. Distinguished from a fetch failure, because it may mean the record was reconciled away.
Elapsed cost and remaining lifetime are older than the refresh interval and are labelled with their observation time rather than shown as current.

elements.name: Identity
elements.description: Name, provider, region, size, and the provider's own identifier.

elements.name: Cost
elements.description: Elapsed cost, the rate it accrues at, and the minimum billable unit that applies.

elements.name: Lifetime
elements.description: Expiry time, time remaining, and the extend control.

elements.name: Enrollment
elements.description: Whether the instance is a trusted node, and if not, why not.

elements.name: Confirm destruction
elements.description: Requires the operator to type the instance name.

claims.statement: Destruction requires typing the instance name and cannot be completed by a single click or by pressing enter on a default-focused control.
claims.rationale: Destruction is irreversible and the machine may be carrying work. A generic confirm dialog is not friction.

claims.statement: No pause, stop or suspend control exists anywhere on this page.
claims.rationale: A stopped instance still bills at the full rate on most providers. Offering the control would imply a saving that does not exist. This mirrors target OT-P0-007.

claims.statement: Queued enrollment is presented as a distinct degraded state, separate from both healthy and failed.
claims.rationale: Enrollment is allowed to lag. Rendering it as an error would train the operator to ignore real errors.

claims.statement: Every cost figure names its amount and its unit, and the minimum billable unit is stated rather than implied.
claims.rationale: Most providers round a partial hour up to a full hour. An operator who does not know that will misread a short-lived instance as cheap.

claims.statement: Every declared state renders a distinct, readable surface.
